correctness.rationale: The exact three-phase decomposition is a bijection. For every fixed quantifier rank \(q\), conditional binomial concentration yields at least \(q\) realizations of each permitted rank/status type; rank and unary type completely determine all atomic formulas, so \(q\)-round EF equivalence proves the uniform-in-path FO mixture. The phase-defining first-order sentence proves convergence necessity; the \(W\) homeomorphism proves sufficiency and the sharp extended-real threshold; disjunctions of phase predicates realize each limiting spectrum point; irrational rotation yields the interval of critical subsequential probabilities. Included checker exhaustively tests 25 small labelled size pairs and evaluates four critical scaling cases, without being used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural quantitative question induced by glut-free persistent semantics is whether uniformly sampled models satisfy an FO convergence law when both levels grow. The result classifies every fixed FO sentence at once, determines a sharp entropy-balance boundary and the complete attainable limit spectrum, and exhibits a density-driven nonconvergence interval despite a convergent level-size ratio. The EF normal form provides information not implied by merely counting finite valuations.
